channel.title: The City Paper Bogotá - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The City Paper Bogotá (thecitypaperbogota.com)

item.title: Ex-FARC admit to recruiting 18,677 children during Colombia conflict | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Former FARC commanders admitted to recruiting 18,677 minors during Colombia’s conflict, acknowledging sexual and reproductive abuses. The confession to the JEP marks a pivotal moment in transitional justice, though victims say full accountability remains unresolved.

item.title: Petro opens consultation on ‘Black Line’ after Colombia court ends protection decree | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Colombia’s President Gustavo Petro has launched consultations with Indigenous communities to draft a new decree protecting the sacred “Black Line” of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta after a court annulled the 2018 regulation recognising 348 ancestral sites.

item.title: Paloma Valencia surge reshapes Colombia race as election season begins
item.description: Colombia’s presidential race entered a decisive new phase this week after Sunday’s inter-party primaries propelled conservative senator Paloma Valencia into the national spotlight and triggered a scramble among political factions to forge alliances ahead of the May 31 election. item.title: Indigenous communities caught in armed clashes in Colombia’s Sierra Nevada | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Clashes between the Clan del Golfo and the Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada trapped Indigenous communities in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, prompting a humanitarian evacuation of nine wounded civilians, including two children, amid rising displacement fears.

item.title: Valencia picks Oviedo as VP to expand Colombia's center-right base | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Conservative presidential candidate Paloma Valencia named economist Juan Daniel Oviedo as her running mate, seeking to broaden the scope of the Centro Democrático's coalition and attract younger urban voters ahead of Colombia’s May 31 presidential election.

item.title: Colombia bars 10 foreigners in single-day crackdown on suspected sex tourism | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Colombia barred 10 foreigners from entering Medellín over suspected sex tourism, as Migración Colombia intensifies controls to combat human trafficking and sexual exploitation linked to international networks.

item.title: Colombia - Ecuador rift widens over cross-border bombings | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Colombia’s Gustavo Petro accuses Ecuador of cross-border bombing, citing 27 bodies, while Daniel Noboa denies claims, deepening a trade-fueled diplomatic crisis and raising risks of escalation.

item.title: Colombia arrests "mastermind" of Ecuador candidate Villavicencio’s murder | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: Colombia arrested alleged Villavicencio mastermind “Lobo Menor” in Bogotá airport, amid tensions with Ecuador over a border explosive, highlighting rising transnational crime and urgent need for coordinated regional security cooperation.

item.title: U.S. prosecutors probe Colombia’s Petro over alleged narco links, NYT reports | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: U.S. prosecutors are investigating Colombia’s President Gustavo Petro over alleged narco links and campaign financing, according to The New York Times, in a case that could affect elections and bilateral relations.

item.title: Colombia mourns 66 dead after military Hercules crash in Putumayo | The City Paper Bogotá
item.description: A Colombian Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crashed near Puerto Leguízamo shortly after take-off, killing 66 of 128 aboard, as authorities investigate the cause and rule out an attack for now.
